 85 medical teams prepared for monsoon flood response
 09-Nov-2026, 19:56 09 Nov 2026, 19:56 Bernama Share The health ministry also identifies healthcare facilities at risk of flooding ahead of the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon.
 As of 6am today, floods were reported in Selangor and Perak, displacing 987 people who are being housed at seven relief centres. (Bernama pic) 
 PUTRAJAYA : The health ministry has prepared 85 emergency medical teams, comprising 387 people, to respond to possible floods during the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon season. 
 In a statement, the ministry said they comprised 36 rapid assessment teams, 34 rapid response teams and 15 mental health and psychosocial support teams.
 “The teams will be mobilised as required to conduct health risk assessments, provide medical services and emergency treatment, carry out surveillance and control of infectious diseases, as well as provide mental health and psychosocial support to flood victims,” it said.
 The ministry has also made 128 vehicles available to support field operations, while flood-related medicine supplies at warehouses operated by concessionaire suppliers remain stable, with stocks estimated to last between one and three months.
 The national crisis response centre has been on alert since Oct 27, continuously monitoring flood situations, healthcare facility preparedness and coordinating response measures with state health departments and relevant agencies.
 The ministry has also identified healthcare facilities at risk of flooding as well as alternative facilities in case of operational disruptions.
 Plans are also in place for the early transfer of high-risk patients, including pregnant women and those requiring haemodialysis.
 As of 6am today, floods were reported in Selangor and Perak, displacing 987 people who are being housed at seven relief centres.
